label: PF Backlog 428
title: A4: EAP delivery manifest + validator/registry + compatibility
body: [A4] EAP as the authoritative delivery/build manifest (composes contracts); versioning + compatibility. Executor role parked.

analysis.implementation_strategy: Extend existing core/artifact_registry.py and core/delivery.py to accept and serve an EAP (Execution Artifact Package) as the authoritative manifest. Add EAP schema versioning in config/file-manifest.json. Register EAP format in config/plugins-registry.json. Expose validator logic under /api/v1/packaging/manifest and /api/v1/evidence/manifest/{run_id}. Reuse core/build_manager.py and core/change_registry.py for compatibility checks across EAP versions.
dependency_findings: REQUIRES core/artifact_registry.py to support structured manifest objects before EAP layer can be authoritative
BLOCKS BI-PF-0399 (Runtime Dependency Compiler) which consumes the EAP manifest as its primary input
BLOCKS BI-PF-0398 (build pipeline) which must emit an EAP as its packaging output
RELATED BI-0171 for knowledge-registry SSOT alignment
RELATED BI-PF-0424 for coordination authority ADR context
conflict_findings: BI-PF-0398 also touches /api/v1/packaging/manifest and core/packaging.py; coordinate manifest schema ownership to avoid concurrent edits on manifest endpoints
BI-PF-0399 also references config/validation-profiles.json; ensure EAP compatibility checker does not conflict with validation-profile changes
duplication_findings: core/artifact_registry.py already provides artifact registration; EAP should compose, not duplicate, this registry
core/delivery.py already handles delivery concerns; EAP manifest layering should sit atop delivery rather than replace it
BI-0171 (knowledge standardization SSOT) may overlap on registry unification; coordinate to avoid duplicate registry work
analysis.rationale: EAP is the authoritative delivery manifest and is a blocking prerequisite for both the build pipeline (A3) and the runtime compiler (A5). It naturally extends the existing artifact_registry and delivery modules. Not a new component because those modules already cover the responsibility boundaries.
assumptions: core/artifact_registry.py already stores sufficient metadata to derive an EAP manifest
The EAP format is a superset of existing file-manifest.json entries, not a separate store
Versioning uses semver with backward-compatible read for at least one prior major version
Validator runs synchronously at packaging time, not as a background process
risks: EAP schema must be stable before dependent items (0398, 0399) build on it; schema churn could cascade
Compatibility rules across EAP versions may be under-specified leading to brittle validators
Existing artifact_registry may not carry sufficient metadata for full EAP composition without modification
evidence: core/artifact_registry.py listed as candidate existing code with high relevance
/api/v1/packaging/manifest already exists and is the natural extension point
config/file-manifest.json already models file-level manifest structure
missing_info: What fields must EAP manifest contain beyond what file-manifest.json provides?
Compatibility policy: how many prior EAP major versions must be readable?
Should EAP be generated eagerly at build time or lazily on first delivery request?
Who owns the EAP schema sign-off (A3/A4 coordination)?

missing: Exact EAP field list beyond file-manifest entries
context_review.reason: Existing artifact_registry, delivery, build_manager, and packaging manifest APIs provide a clear extension path; the missing items are policy decisions, not architectural blockers.

dependencies.required_state: EAP manifest schema approved and validator implemented
EAP manifest endpoint serving structured EAP objects

brief.problem: Editions need one authoritative delivery/build manifest to compose and ship consistently.
brief.what_adds: A4 — EAP (manifest) composes contracts; validator/registry; versioning + compatibility. Executor role is parked.
brief.why: Single source of truth for what ships per edition, enabling compatibility and repeatable builds.
brief.who_feels: PF platform maintainers, workers, and customers.

objective: A4 — EAP (manifest) composes contracts; validator/registry; versioning + compatibility. Executor role is parked.
approach: Define EAP as the authoritative manifest composing A1 contracts; add a validator + registry with version/compat rules.
